Arrive at Bogotá International Airport, where you'll be met and transferred to your hotel.

The Spanish founded Bogotá in the 16th century on the site of earlier Indigenous settlements. The city's name is thought to come from that of a Chibcha leader.

Today Bogotá is a large city with historic neighbourhoods, museums, restaurants, cafés and modern visitor districts.

After check-in and a short rest, take a sightseeing tour of La Candelaria, the historic centre. Its colonial houses, churches and narrow streets have been preserved.

A main stop is the Gold Museum, with a rich collection of pre-Hispanic gold objects and more than 20,000 exhibits from the pre-Columbian era.

Next is Casa de la Moneda, the old mint, founded in the 17th century and housed in a colonial mansion.

Nearby is the Fernando Botero Museum. The artist donated a large collection of his work to the city. The museum also displays works by Dalí and other European artists.

After visiting the museums, stroll through Plaza de Bolívar, Bogotá's main square, where you'll find a monument to the first president and the cathedral.

If the tour passes the presidential palace around 17:00, you may see the changing of the guard.

Return to the hotel.
